final_message:
All five versions are complete and verified. Cleaned up all test artifacts.

## Algorithm

For each JSON Line: parse the top-level object structurally (so nested `account`/`tags`/`type`/`meta` keys inside `extra` and `meta.extra` are ignored), extract `account`, `type`, `amount`, `currency`, `tags`, `meta.channel`; skip if type is `void` or a tag decodes to `test`; convert the decimal string to hundredths, then `usd = hundredths * rate / 1_000_000` in integer arithmetic, apply sign (`credit`/`refund` positive, `debit` negative), and accumulate per-channel and per-account totals. Finally sort channels by byte order and take the top 10 accounts by sum desc / id asc.

All parsers are hand-written byte scanners (no JSON library), with escape decoding (`\"`, `\\`, `\/`, `\n`, `\uXXXX`, surrogate pairs) done lazily only when a string actually contains a backslash. Strings are compared/aggregated as byte ranges. Only counted rows create account entries, and phantom entries from skipped rows are filtered by count.

## Per-language speed choices

- **C++**: whole-file `fread` into one buffer, raw `const char*` scanning, `std::string_view` keys into the buffer, FNV open-addressed hash for accounts (no per-line string allocation), depth-scan skipping of unknown values, binary stdout.
- **Java**: `Files.readAllBytes`, static byte-array scanner with hot loops localized to registers, custom open-addressing byte-range account map (no per-transaction `String`s except new channels/accounts), depth-scan `skipValue` with inlined string skipping, one buffered write.
- **C#**: `File.ReadAllBytes` + `fixed` raw pointers, native scratch buffer for decoded strings, custom int[] open-addressing map over a byte arena, depth-scan skipping, direct stdout stream write.
- **Go**: `os.ReadFile`, local-index byte scanner, `map[string]int` with Go's zero-allocation `m[string(b)]` lookups, byte arena for account names, depth-scan skipping, single output buffer.
- **JavaScript**: `readFileSync` Buffer + byte-index parser, typed-array open-addressing account map (Int32 slots, Float64 sums, Uint8 arena) avoiding strings/Map for the hot path, depth-scan skipping, one `write`.

An early, correctness-preserving optimization replacing recursive value skipping with a depth/string-aware byte scan cut Java parsing from ~3.0 s to ~1.5 s and improved every version.

## Verification

Tested with:
- all three provided samples (exact byte match, LF endings),
- 8 randomized 3,000-line datasets with shuffled keys/whitespace, escaped keys and values (`\u0061ccount`, `\u0074est`, escaped channels/types/currencies/amounts), surrogate pairs, nested decoy objects/arrays, compared against an independent Python `json`-based reference,
- an explicit edge file (escaped keys, amount `12`/`12.5`/`12.05`, tie-breaking at equal sums, void/test filtering) and a rates-only file with zero transactions,
- a 1,000,000-transaction (422 MB) input, where all five produced byte-identical output.

| Version | Samples | Random + edge | 422 MB synthetic |
|---|---|---|---|
| C++ | s1, s2, s3 pass | pass | ~1.7 s |
| Java | s1, s2, s3 pass | pass | ~2.4 s |
| C# | s1, s2, s3 pass | pass | ~1.7 s |
| Go | s1, s2, s3 pass | pass | ~1.8 s |
| JavaScript | s1, s2, s3 pass | pass | ~2.7 s |

(Timings are noise-affected wall time on this shared machine; all outputs were identical.)

request.prompt:
You are writing five versions of the same program, in C++, Java, C#, Go and JavaScript, for a comparison of
how fast and how memory-hungry each version is.

The task is described in SPEC.md in this folder. The folder samples/ holds example inputs (`*.in`), each with
the exact expected output (`*.out`).

Each language has its own folder with a starting file and a `build.cmd`. The benchmark builds every program with
these same build scripts and flags, whatever you change in them. Write these programs:

1. `cpp/main.cpp` (more `.cpp` and header files in `cpp/` are fine): C++20, built by `cpp\build.cmd` with
   Microsoft Visual C++ 19.40 (Visual Studio 2022) and `/O2 /GL /EHsc /std:c++20`. Standard library only, plus
   nlohmann/json 3.12 (`#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>`, already in `cpp/include/`). Run as
   `cpp\solution.exe INPUT_PATH`.
2. `java/src/Main.java` (more `.java` files in `java/src/` are fine): Java 23, built by `java\build.cmd` with
   `javac`. Java SE only, plus Jackson 2.22 (core, databind and annotations, already in `java/lib/`). Run as
   `java\run.cmd INPUT_PATH`, which runs `java -cp "out;lib\*" Main` with the default JVM settings.
3. `csharp/Program.cs` (more `.cs` files in `csharp/` are fine): C# 12 on .NET 8, built in Release by
   `csharp\build.cmd`. Base class library only. You may change properties in `csharp/solution.csproj`, but do not
   add package references. Run as `csharp\out\solution.exe INPUT_PATH`.
4. `go/main.go` (more `.go` files in `go/` are fine): Go 1.27, built by `go\build.cmd`. Standard library only.
   Run as `go\solution.exe INPUT_PATH`.
5. `js/main.js`: JavaScript on Node.js 22, with no build step. Built-in Node modules only; no npm packages. Run as
   `node js\main.js INPUT_PATH`.

Each program reads the input file whose path is its first argument (SPEC.md says if a task takes more
arguments) and writes the answer to standard output exactly as SPEC.md describes.

Your goals, in order:

1. Every version must print the correct output for any valid input as SPEC.md defines it, not only for the
   samples.
2. Make each version as fast as you can. Write each one the way a skilled developer in that language would
   write fast code, using that language's own strengths.

Use a single thread and a single process unless SPEC.md says otherwise. Do not precompute or embed answers,
start other programs, or read any file other than the input. Python 3.13 (`C:\Python313\python.exe`) is
available if you want it for testing, but not as part of any program.

The programs will be run on Windows 11 on a 16-core laptop, on larger inputs of the same kind; SPEC.md gives
the benchmark size. Build and test all five versions against every sample before you finish. Work only inside
this folder, and take at most about 60 minutes. Other programs run on this machine at the same time: never stop
a process you did not start yourself, so do not kill processes by name (for example `taskkill /IM java.exe` or
`Stop-Process -Name node`); stop only your own processes, by process ID.

When you are done, reply with a short summary: the algorithm, the main choices you made for speed in each
version, and which samples each version passes.
